messages:
anil-customer: Hey team — after our IdP cert rotation last night, SSO is failing for all users. Error in our logs: 

```
SAMLResponse validation failed: SubjectConfirmationData Recipient mismatch. Expected https://app.customerco.com/_sso/redwood but got https://app.customerco.com/_sso/redwood/
Status: urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:status:Responder
```

We didn't change our SP config on our side. Any obvious checks?

Lina (Support): Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste the exact ACS/consumer URL configured in your IdP metadata and what the SP (Redwood) is getting as the Recipient? Also, is your IdP sending signed metadata after the rotation?

anil-customer: ACS we published in metadata is `https://app.customerco.com/_sso/redwood` (no trailing slash). The SAML response (decoded) shows Recipient with trailing slash. Quick decode we ran:

```
echo 'BASE64_SAML_RESPONSE' | base64 -d | xmllint --format - | sed -n '1,120p'
# ... shows <SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://app.customerco.com/_sso/redwood/" NotOnOrAfter="..." />
```

maya-idp-admin: we rotated the signing cert and updated metadata. I double-checked our metadata.xml and the ACS entry was emitted with a trailing slash — we generate with a templated base URL that sometimes includes a slash. I thought SPs are resilient to that but apparently Redwood is strict.

Sam (SRE): Quick theory: We do strict recipient equality checks in the SAML consumer service for SubjectConfirmationData. Historically we tolerated trailing slash differences but a recent edge change enabled path normalization at the LB which removed/re-added trailing slashes inconsistently. That can flip what the SP sees as the ACS vs what IdP sent. Two things to check now:
- Have you got any proxies/ingress rewriting path? (nginx, ALB path normalization)
- Can you share the raw SAMLRequest/Response for a failed login so we can inspect Recipient/Destination fields?

anil-customer: We do have an AWS ALB in front of app. No intentional rewriting but we recently added a rule to redirect to HTTPS which might be doing something. Sharing a redacted base64 payload now.

Lina (Support): Thanks. If you can, decode and grep for Recipient/Destination inside the Response and paste the lines. Also include the SP entityID configured in your IdP (sometimes the entityID encodes a trailing slash variant).

anil-customer: Pasted fragments:
```
<Assertion ...>
  <SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://app.customerco.com/_sso/redwood/" NotOnOrAfter="2025-10-02T12:34:56Z"/>
</Assertion>
<Response Destination="https://app.customerco.com/_sso/redwood" ...>
```

So weird — Response Destination no slash, SubjectConfirmationData Recipient has slash.

maya-idp-admin: That explains it — some IdP stacks compute Recipient from the ACS template and some libraries append slash when building SubjectConfirmationData. We can patch our templating to canonicalize. Two mitigation paths:
1) Update IdP metadata to use the exact ACS with trailing slash to match what the IdP emits (quick but pins to trailing-slash form).
2) Update SP (Redwood) to accept both variants (preferred long-term), or adjust LB to ensure consistent URL normalization.

Sam (SRE): Operational steps for us to help debug and mitigate from the Redwood side:
- I'll add logging to surface the exact Recipient and Destination values we receive (already captured in logs but make it explicit).
- We can add a temporary config toggle to allow trailing-slash tolerant recipient check for your org only while you update IdP metadata. This is a narrow mitigation we can roll back.
- Confirm whether the ALB is altering the path: run `curl -i -sS -L -o /dev/null -w "%{url_effective}\n" https://app.customerco.com/_sso/redwood` against the ALB and origin to see canonical URL.

anil-customer: Ran the curl. It returns `https://app.customerco.com/_sso/redwood/` (ALB adds slash). Ugh.

Lina (Support): OK, two-pronged plan: Maya — can you update metadata to include ACS with trailing slash as an alias and re-publish? Anil — I'll open a temporary org-scoped toggle for Recipient tolerance and keep it short-lived. After you confirm IdP metadata change works we'll remove the toggle.

maya-idp-admin: Will push updated metadata with both ACS variants and re-sign it. Also checking cert chain: we rotated to a cert signed by an internal intermediate; I want to be sure Redwood picks it up. Can you confirm you fetched metadata after rotation?

Lina (Support): We fetched the metadata you uploaded at 2025-10-02T03:00:00Z and validated signatures; there was an alert showing the cert in the metadata matched the new public key. If you rotated TLS certs for the IdP host as well, we recommend verifying the full TLS chain with `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect idp.example.com:443` — we've seen customers with missing intermediate certs cause signature verification oddities.

deploy-bot: Deploy job #3421 for org customerco rolled: feature/saml-trailing-slash-tolerance -> staging successful

Sam (SRE): Toggle is live on a canary for your org. Please test a few users and paste SAML debug lines if any failures persist. Note: toggle only relaxes trailing-slash equality for SubjectConfirmationData Recipient check, everything else (signature, audience) still enforced.

anil-customer: Tested with three users, 2/3 succeed now. The failing one returns `SubjectConfirmationData NotOnOrAfter` slightly in the past — clock skew on the client side (desktop set to wrong timezone). So looks like trailing-slash was the main blocker.

maya-idp-admin: Updated metadata is live and verified. Once you flip the toggle off can you confirm log count is clean? We'll retire the trailing-slash variant in a week.

Lina (Support): We'll monitor and remove the toggle after 48 hours of stable sign-ins. I'll also open an internal KB to document: "Common SAML Recipient mismatches — trailing slash, proxy normalization, cert chain checks" with the exact commands we used.

anil-customer: Thanks all — appreciate the fast turnaround. Please keep me posted before you remove the toggle so we can ensure all users migrated.

Sam (SRE): Noted — will post here before rollback. Closing interim incident once toggle is removed and logs are green.

Lina (Support): Closing thread for now, will update KB and ping you before the final rollback. :thumbsup:
